questions.question: What invariant protects an ML system from silent training-serving mismatch?
options: Training and serving consume data with explicit lineage, time semantics, and reproducible transformations
Every feature is recomputed from scratch for each request
Every event is processed by a streaming engine
Training uses the largest possible historical table
questions.explanation: The invariant makes a feature traceable, reconstructible, and comparable across offline and online consumers. The implementation can still be batch, streaming, or hybrid.

questions.question: A purchase occurred at 09:55 but reached the pipeline at 10:07. Which time should define a 30-minute historical feature window?
options: Ingestion time, 10:07
Event time, 09:55
The time a model is retrained
Whichever clock is easier to query
questions.explanation: Event time represents when the business action happened. Ingestion time is still useful for measuring source delay and replay progress.

questions.question: When is batch usually the better initial choice?
options: When hourly or daily freshness meets the product need and reproducible runs matter
When every decision must use the latest event within seconds
When events can arrive late
When feature values need lineage
questions.explanation: Late events and lineage occur in every processing mode. Batch is the simpler baseline when its scheduled freshness meets the actual product SLO.

questions.question: Why does point-in-time training data matter?
options: It reconstructs only the information available at the historical prediction moment
It guarantees all features have zero missing values
It removes the need to store event time
It lets the model use the eventual label as a feature
questions.explanation: Point-in-time joins prevent future leakage, so offline examples reflect the information the production model could have seen.

questions.question: A schema change makes a critical input ambiguous. What is the safest first action?
options: Quarantine or stop publication for the incompatible records, preserve reason codes, and identify affected consumers
Fill the missing field with zero and continue
Retrain immediately with the changed data
Delete raw events so the old schema cannot be replayed
questions.explanation: A contract gate prevents a plausible-looking but incompatible value from reaching features. Raw evidence and reason codes support a scoped repair.

questions.question: Which backfill response best limits risk after a bounded duplicate-event defect?
options: Rebuild the affected event-time interval into a candidate version, validate it, then atomically publish compatible offline and online views
Overwrite the online store immediately and leave training data unchanged
Reprocess only today's ingestion-time partition without checking event time
Disable deduplication so the stream can catch up
questions.explanation: A bounded, versioned rebuild repairs the known interval while preserving validation and avoiding training-serving skew.
